info.name: Studzee Backend API
info.description:
Backend service for content delivery and notifications. Covers health checks, public content, PDF listing, device registration for push, the Clerk webhook, and the admin surface for documents, notifications, email and users.

The notification service was merged into this backend, so the endpoints that used to sit behind /noti/api are now served here under /notifications, /admin and /webhooks.

SETUP

1. Set baseUrl if the API is not on http://localhost:4000.
2. For authenticated and admin routes, set clerkToken. Use a Clerk session JWT, or for local work paste the DEV_TOKEN value from BACKEND/.env, which grants admin rights and is ignored outside NODE_ENV=development.
3. Run Get Paginated Content once. It saves the first document id into the documentId variable, so every request that needs an id works without copying values by hand.

request.description: Root route. Returns the service name and a map of the main endpoints, useful for confirming which build is deployed.
Checks if the application is running.
Simple health check endpoint for Render or other hosting platforms. This is the URL the heartbeat job pings.

Checks every backing store the service needs: MongoDB for content, Postgres for users and notifications, and Redis for caching.

Each check issues a real round trip rather than reading a driver connection flag, so it cannot report healthy while a store has stopped answering. Probes run in parallel with a 2 second timeout each.

Returns 200 with every check ok, or 503 naming the store that failed.
The fixed topic registry in display order. Public. Use these keys for filtering and for labelling sections.
Retrieve documents created during the current IST day, which runs from 18:30 UTC to 18:30 UTC.

query.description: Optional registry key filter. Unknown keys answer 400.

request.description: Retrieve a paginated list of documents, optionally scoped to one topic from the fixed registry. Items carry their topic key so clients can group a page locally.

exec: // Saves the first document id into the documentId collection variable,
// so the requests that need an id work without copying values by hand.
console.log("no documents returned, run npm run seed first")

variable.description: Taken from the documentId collection variable, which Get Paginated Content sets for you.

request.description: Retrieve a complete document by its ID. Requires authentication. Documents carrying an unlockPoints cost answer 403 with code CONTENT_LOCKED when the caller has fewer points.
Retrieve a paginated list of documents with uploaded PDFs, flattened to one entry per PDF.

Register the caller's device for push notifications, or attach another device token to an existing registration. The Clerk identity comes from the bearer token, never from the body. Tokens are deduplicated, so re-registering the same device does not create a second entry.

Replaces POST /noti/api/register from the old notification service.

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.
Points, level and next level, streaks, active days, earned badges plus the full catalog with awarded flags, and recent attempts. Requires authentication.

Grades a quiz server side against the stored answers (responses maps each quiz question key to the chosen option index), records the attempt, awards points as a delta over prior best for that content, and updates streaks and badges. 404 when the content has no quiz.

Ask the in app support assistant one question. Requires a signed in Clerk user, not an admin.

The assistant answers only from a knowledge base built out of the help material, the level and badge registries, and the study material catalogue. It has no access to the caller's account and cannot read progress, history, downloads or email. It answers about Studzee and nothing else, and it will not describe how the service is built or hosted.

The answer is plain prose with **bold** and *italic* and nothing else. No tables, lists, headings, code fences, em dashes or emoji.

`history` is held by the client and capped at 12 turns, of which the last 6 reach the model. No transcript is stored on the server.

When nothing in the knowledge base matches, this still returns 200 with an email referral and an empty `sources` array, and no model call is made.

`remaining` is how many questions the caller has left today. Over the allowance is 429 AI_QUOTA_EXCEEDED; Redis being unreachable is 503 AI_QUOTA_UNAVAILABLE, because the spend ceiling fails closed.

The reply is not streamed, so set a client timeout far longer than for any other endpoint.

Returns 503 AI_DISABLED while AI_ENABLED is false.

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute, on top of the per account daily allowance.

request.description:
Receives Clerk events. Only user.created is acted on, which sends the welcome email.

This endpoint takes no user token. The svix signature is its only authentication, and the handler verifies the raw request bytes. A request sent from Postman without valid svix headers signed by CLERK_WEBHOOK_SIGNING_SECRET will correctly return 400. Use the Clerk dashboard's webhook tester for a real end to end check.

The endpoint always answers 2xx once the signature verifies, including when the welcome email fails, because a non 2xx makes Clerk redeliver and resend the email.

Create a new document. Requires the admin role.

Note that `content` is structured, either an array of sections or an object. It is not a plain string.

exec: console.log("documentId set to the new document " + body.doc._id)

variable.description: Taken from the documentId collection variable, which Get Paginated Content sets for you.

request.description:
Update an existing document. Requires the admin role.

The body is a partial document validated against the same schema as create, so any subset of the document fields is accepted and at least one field is required.

request.description: Delete a document by its ID. Requires the admin role.

formdata.description: Image file (JPG, PNG, or WebP, max 10MB)

request.description:
Upload the cover image for a document. Replaces any existing image. Requires the admin role.

IMPORTANT: in the Body tab, the form-data row named file is only a placeholder. You must click Select Files and choose an actual file, otherwise Postman sends nothing and the request fails with 400 No file uploaded. The field name must be file.

variable.description: Taken from the documentId collection variable, which Get Paginated Content sets for you.

request.description:
Attach a PDF to a document. Documents hold an array of PDFs, so this appends rather than replaces. Requires the admin role.

IMPORTANT: in the Body tab, click Select Files on the form-data row named file and choose a real PDF. A row with no file attached sends nothing and fails with 400 No file uploaded. The field name must be file.

Broadcast a push notification to every registered device. Requires the admin role.

Messages are chunked to the Expo limit of 100 per request, so a broadcast larger than that is split across several calls. Tokens Expo reports as DeviceNotRegistered are pruned immediately.

Returns 200 when every message was accepted and 207 when the broadcast was only partially delivered, with sent, failed and prunedTokens counts in the body.

Replaces POST /noti/api/admin/notification/send.

Rate limit: 20 requests per minute.

Send to the devices belonging to a named set of users. `emails` is required and must be non empty whenever `sendToAll` is false, which the schema enforces. Returns 404 when none of the named users have a registered device.

query.description: One of createdAt, status, sentBy. Anything else falls back to createdAt.

request.description:
Paginated history of sent notifications. Requires the admin role.

Replaces GET /noti/api/admin/notifications.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Send a transactional email. Requires the admin role.

`body` is an HTML fragment composed by the caller and dropped into the shared template. Recipients are sent as bcc, so one broadcast does not disclose the list to everyone on it.

Attachments are fetched by the mail transport at send time, so every entry in `pdfUrls` must be https on a host listed in EMAIL_ATTACHMENT_HOSTS, with at most 10 per message. Anything else returns a failure without sending.

Returns 502 when the transport rejects the message. Replaces POST /noti/api/admin/email/send.

Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

Paginated history of sent emails. Requires the admin role.

Replaces GET /noti/api/admin/email/logs.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Paginated list of registered users. Requires the admin role.

Replaces GET /noti/api/admin/users.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Every registered email address, for populating a recipient picker. Requires the admin role.

Replaces GET /noti/api/admin/emails.

Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Write a whole study document from a title, a brief, or both. At least one of the two is required, checked before a model call is paid for.

This is the only generator with no `contentId`. Nothing existing is being derived from, so the reviewer is the only accuracy check there is.

Supply `title` or `topic` and they are honoured exactly. Leave them out and the model writes the title and picks the topic from the fixed six key registry, which is the case this endpoint exists for: paste material in and let it be named and filed. `brief` takes up to 12000 characters, so a whole article fits.

Three model calls deep, the body first and then the quiz and the notes against that body. Budget around a minute.

Returns 201 with a pending draft carrying a complete document. Approving it creates the document and pushes a notification.

Content blocks are validated against the five types the client renders, which are text, list, table, formula and code. An invented block type is rejected with AI_INVALID_OUTPUT rather than rendering as a gap on the screen.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

Draft quiz questions from a document that already exists.

The generated quiz is validated against the same QuizItemSchema the document schema uses, so every item already has at least two options and an `ans` matching one of them character for character.

Approving appends the questions to the document's quiz under fresh keys rather than merging by key, because the generator numbers from q1 every time and merging would overwrite the existing questions.

`count` is 1 to 15 and defaults to 5.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

item.name: Generate a Summary and Key Notes

request.description:
Draft a summary and key notes for a document that already exists.

Approving replaces the summary and merges the key notes, with the generated ones winning a heading collision. Merging rather than replacing means approving notes cannot silently delete notes written by hand.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

Draft a quest from a document that already exists.

The model writes the title, description and questions only. The type, gems, window and pass mark come from this request, and the assembled quest is parsed by CreateQuestSchema, the same schema POST /admin/quests uses, before the draft is stored, so approval cannot fail on shape.

`passScore` is clamped to the number of questions the model actually returned. Asking for three and getting two would otherwise produce a quest nobody can complete. Left out, it defaults to sixty percent of the questions, rounded up.

`type` is mcq, scq, fill_blank or read_blog. A read_blog quest carries no questions and keeps the contentId; a graded quest is self contained.

Quest.title is unique, so approval pre-checks and returns 409 QUEST_TITLE_TAKEN on a clash, which is resolved by approving again with an overrides.title.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

Draft push copy for a document or a quest. Drafts only, it sends nothing. Approving the draft is the send.

`kind` is content or quest. `id` is a Mongo document id or a quest cuid, so it is not constrained to a Mongo shape.

Title is capped at 60 characters and message at 160, which is what a phone shows before truncating.

A nightly job at 01:00 UTC drafts these automatically for material published and quests opened in the previous day, skipping any subject that already has a notification draft in any state.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 10 requests per minute.

Paginated review queue, newest first.

Filter by `status` (pending, approved, rejected) and by `kind` (document, quiz, key_notes, quest, notification). Both are optional.

A draft that failed to apply stays pending with the reason in `error`, so filtering on pending surfaces retryable work as well as unreviewed work.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

One draft with its full payload. This is what you read before approving.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 30 requests per minute.

Apply the draft. This is the only path by which a generated payload becomes something a student can see.

WARNING. Approving a document draft publishes it AND pushes a notification to every registered device. Approving a notification draft sends that push. Neither can be undone from this API.

`overrides` is merged over the stored payload before it applies, which is how a title clash or a bad question is fixed without a separate edit endpoint. The merged result is re-validated against the schema the draft was generated under, so an override cannot introduce a shape the generator would have rejected.

Each kind dispatches to the service the matching admin route already uses: document to POST /admin/documents, quiz and key_notes to PUT /admin/documents/:id, quest to the service POST /admin/quests uses, and notification to the send and audit pair POST /admin/notifications/send uses.

409 DRAFT_NOT_PENDING if it was already approved or rejected. 409 QUEST_TITLE_TAKEN on a duplicate quest title. 400 DRAFT_INVALID if the payload failed validation after overrides.

A failed apply leaves the draft pending with the reason in `error` rather than losing it, so a transient failure is retryable.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 20 requests per minute.

Mark the draft rejected with an optional reason, up to 500 characters.

A rejected notification draft still counts for the nightly job's dedupe check, so rejecting one stops it being redrafted tomorrow.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 20 requests per minute.

Rebuild every knowledge base passage and re-embed it. The table is deleted and rewritten, so a passage removed from support.md or a document deleted from the collection disappears here too.

Run after editing src/services/ai/kb/support.md, after changing a level or badge, and after a content import. Nothing reindexes on its own, so a support.md edit does nothing until this runs.

The response `index` lists every passage stored, without its text or its vector. The command line equivalent, npm run ai:reindex, additionally writes src/services/ai/kb/KB-CONTENTS.md, a readable inventory of the whole corpus. This route does not write that file, because it runs inside a container where there is nowhere useful to put it.

Requires the admin role. Rate limit: 2 requests per minute.

variable.description: API root. Change this to point at a deployed environment.

Bearer token for authenticated and admin routes. Paste a Clerk session JWT, or for local work paste the DEV_TOKEN value from BACKEND/.env, which grants admin rights and is ignored outside NODE_ENV=development.
Set automatically by Get Paginated Content and by Create Document. Used by every request that takes a document id.
